title: Staged taper rollout: visual journey and operator controls prototype
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Design a compact, operator-friendly flow for staged traffic rollouts that combines a timeline view, a granular taper control, and a rollback chimney visual. The goal is to let SREs and product owners safely author canary/A-B experiments with explicit safety gates (metrics-based pauses) while making the traffic curve and expected cost impact visible at every step. This prototype emphasizes: 1) an accessible single-pane flow for creating and editing a staged rollout; 2) a tactile taper slider that maps percent traffic to latency/cost estimates; 3) inline safety gates with suggested thresholds pulled from historical workload profiles; 4) a compact rollback chimney showing delta between current stable and candidate variants and the predicted user-exposure during rollback.

Scope: mid-fidelity clickable prototype of the full flow (create, simulate, preview, commit), plus a set of micro-interactions for the taper editor and safety gate editor. Not in scope: backend integration for telemetry; we’ll stub data with synthetic traces.

Success criteria: usability test mean task time under 4 minutes for "create a 5-step staged rollout"; participants correctly use safety gates in 90% of attempts; clear comprehension of cost delta in prototype post-test survey +1.0 (Likert).

decisions: Use banded timeline (single-row) to surface dense rollout steps without vertical scroll.
Expose a taper slider (percentage curve editor) rather than manual numeric step entry to reduce operator error.
Show inline cost and latency delta estimates per step using synthetic workload profiles; label clearly as 'estimate' until telemetry-backed API is available.
Rollback chimney is read-only in create flow but editable in 'edit active rollout' mode to avoid accidental exposure edits during deploy.
Safety gate suggestions generated from 95th/99th percentile historic traces; user can accept or tune thresholds.
Accessibility: slider must support keyboard arrow nudges by 0.5% and provide aria-live updates for screen readers.
